items.title: European Economics: Fiscal Policy vs. Higher Yields
items.summary: A directional turn in European fiscal policy remains a building block of our growth outlook for the next few years, but we've revised our outlook for policy rates and EGB yields higher, with the constraining effects becoming more tangible as the debt stock has to be rolled over.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: Key Takeaways, Pt. 2
items.summary: We offer the second installment of key takeaways from our China Conference in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with notes on names including Anjoy Foods, China Northern Rare Earth High-Tech, Han's Laser Technology, Las Vegas Sands, Meitu, OmniVision and Sinotruk.

items.title: Robust UK GDP Suggests Stronger Case for a December Hike
items.summary: UK third-quarter GDP grew a solid 0.7%, continuing a run of good growth, with more volatile monthly data also suggesting steady growth ahead. We currently expect rates to be held steady in December and raised in February, but the print suggests back-to-back hikes are now more likely.

items.title: Turkey Economics: Targets Revised, Stance Unchanged
items.summary: Turkey's central bank raised its inflation forecast for the end of 2026 to 29.5% and revised targets through 2028, even as domestic demand cools and underlying inflation slows. Persistent supply shocks are keeping upside risks elevated, warranting a continued tight monetary-policy stance.

items.title: Key Takeaways From Our 15th Annual FinTech Conference
items.summary: Our 15th annual FinTech Conference spotlighted that FinTech appears to be entering its next phase, with AI usage moving from cost reduction toward revenue generation. Rising complexity is making scale, trust, proprietary data, regulatory infrastructure, and distribution more valuable.

items.title: U.S. Economics: Whipsawed by Waller
items.summary: In just one day, Fedspeak combined with another hot core CPI reading led to a substantial repricing in near-term rate hike expectations. Overnight, comments from Governor Waller explicitly put the possibility of a 50-basis-point December hike on the table. We consider what may lie ahead.

items.title: Citi Internet Insight Series: Agentic Commerce's Inflection Point
items.summary: Following conversations with executives at Publicis and ReFiBuy.ai, we see agentic commerce as reaching an inflection point, with AI increasingly influencing product discovery, and note the potential for agentic commerce to be a meaningful contributor to ecommerce growth in 2027.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: Key Takeaways, Pt. 1
items.summary: We offer the first installment of key takeaways from our China Conference in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with notes on names including CLP Holdings, Eastroc Beverage, Galaxy Entertainment, HUTCHMED, Leapmotor, Sunny Optical and Yadea Group.

items.title: Data-Center Buildouts: Getting More Expensive? Yes. Over? No.
items.summary: In the short term, sentiment-driven volatility and AI concerns are generating mixed market signals about data-center buildouts. But over the long term, a pause today may result in more transparent, responsible, and sustainable AI advancement. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: CPI Shows Signs of Possible Pass-Through as Energy Prices Fall
items.summary: Core CPI rose 0.296% month over month in October, another stronger-than-expected print. Strength in the details may reflect pass-through of higher energy costs. We continue to expect a 25-basis-point December hike, but risks of a 50-bp hike have risen.  We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: North America Transportation:  Fundamentals Look Strong
items.summary: Transportation earnings were broadly strong, with mostly upbeat outlooks, helped by supportive supply-demand fundamentals. Yet many stocks remain range-bound and well off 52-week highs — an attractive entry point, we believe, into year's end and 2027. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: NVIDIA Investors Will Focus on Multiple Topics
items.summary: We expect a modest EPS beat from Nvidia, with higher sales offset by lower gross margins due to HBM price increases. We review topics of likely interest to investors, including the question of long-term leadership stability. We trim our target price for Buy-rated NVDA to $285.

items.title: Essential Energy: Imagining a Post-Conflict Oil World
items.summary: In a post-conflict oil world with prices in the mid-70s, Global IOCs could offer 7-8% free cash flow yield and, for a time, 4-5% in real growth. This all-in return looks comfortably above the sector's cost of equity and could help begin to reverse the group's 10-year secular de-rating.

items.title: Deep Dive: What's Ahead for Estée Lauder in China?
items.summary: We offer takeaways from Estée Lauder's Capital Markets Experience and conduct a Deep Dive into its business in China and Travel Retail. We reiterate our Buy rating and raise our target price to $132, as we see meaningful progress under EL's Beauty Reimagined strategy.

items.title: Mexico Telecom: Diversification, Dividends and Consolidation
items.summary: Our Deep Dive into Mexico telecommunications sees strong competitive dynamics as likely to persist in a decelerating market, thus intensifying the impacts and compounding the effects. As explored herein, we expect cable market consolidation to become an industry theme.

items.title: China Economics: AI Exports Stay Strong But Trade Headwinds Build
items.summary: China’s export engine remained resilient in October, with AI-related products driving another month of strong growth. We see the near-term trade environment as staying supportive, but headwinds could intensify in 2027. We expect export growth to slow toward 8%, and note trade-policy risks.

items.title: Global Equity Strategy: Reassessing the Balance of Risks
items.summary: After a period of index-level calm and violent rotation, global equities have tumbled in a more broad-based fashion. Against this backdrop, we make several changes to our recommendations. Our market targets remain constructive given three factors, which we explore in this presentation.

items.title: World Radar Screen: November Update
items.summary: Dispersion rose sharply in October, leaving the MSCI World Value/Momentum strategy in decline (-9.9%), along with most developed regions. The Developed Markets reversal was driven by bottom-decile rallies; in a contrast, declining bottom-decile stocks supported Emerging Markets.

items.title: Industrials' Upcycle Looks Intact Despite Near-Term Volatility
items.summary: Despite post-election volatility associated with data-center concerns, Industrials earnings were largely aligned with our expectations. We think a widespread curtailing of data-center-related construction activity is unlikely and see industrial “broadening” as an intact, ongoing narrative.

items.title: North America Railroads: Strong Fundamentals Vs. Merger Hurdles
items.summary: Rails sentiment has seesawed given investors' competing views of the UP-NS merger. Following third-quarter results, we think it's important to step back and note that fundamentals look encouraging, with some of the strongest environments for volume, pricing, and operations seen in years.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of Muyuan Foods at Buy
items.summary: We initiate coverage of Muyuan A- and H-shares at Buy. The company looks best placed for a longer, calmer hog cycle ahead, backed by structural cost leadership, self-sufficient breeding, and a slaughtering business that is increasingly smoothing earnings. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: China Sees Rising Near-Term Risks of “Bad Inflation”
items.summary: China's October inflation data came in mixed, with another CPI miss but a PPI beat. Near term, we see rising risks of “bad inflation,” tilted to the upside for PPI and the downside for CPI. But these inflation prints don't alter our expectation that deflationary risks will return in 2027.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Good Time Market’s Got the Blues
items.summary: For much of the past year, the credit cycle has shown signs of aging, balanced by factors that kept that cycle expanding, such as the AI buildout and a light regulatory touch. But the midterms' historic blue wave could shift these factors in the coming years, accelerating the cycle’s turn.

items.title: FX Basis Quarterly: Staying Paid After the Risk-Off
items.summary: We expect the recent volatility in the XCCY basis to normalize after this risk-off move comes to an end. Entering year end, we offer strategies given our thesis that the Fed will keep reserves ample next year. We also discuss our updated view of the debt ceiling through 2027.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Struggling to Chase the UST Rally
items.summary: The near-term road to lower yields runs through a continued risk-off. We take off our January receive leg of our Dec/Jan FOMC flattener and go outright paid Dec FOMC. In the long end, we no longer expect Treasury to reduce 20y and 30y supply, although the tail risk remains.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Buying Risk-Off Insurance
items.summary: POLLS suggests staying out of U.S. equities until late November and other warning signals may soon suggest the market isn't in the mood for a typical post-midterms rally, as the blue sweep is compounding AI concerns. We offer tactics to consider in case the AI bubble has already burst.

items.title: Global Commodities: When Weather Meets Geopolitics
items.summary: We're initiating long trade ideas in corn, soybeans and sugar, as well as a long strangle options strategy in cocoa. As explored herein, we remain bullish on agricultural commodities with exposure to energy markets and see the market as approaching an inflection point in the El Niño story.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Headwind or Hurricane?
items.summary: Post-midterms volatility has investors on edge while putting policy back at center stage. The semis-led selloff brought AI and data-center buildouts into the spotlight; we expect compromise will ultimately prevail, but a heighted volatility backdrop is likely as we grind toward year's end.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Volume Outpaces Price
items.summary: Despite market concerns triggering the latest AI-trade correction, recent releases have helped rebuild the performance lead of frontier proprietary models over open-weight alternatives, supporting adoption gains as advances toward recursive self-improvement accelerate frontier progress.

items.title: North America Midstream & Energy Infrastructure: Blue to Red
items.summary: The blue wave brought a very red week for Midstream and broader energy, which saw the worst weekly performance since Liberation Day. Despite macro pressures, earnings were largely constructive, with boosts to '26 guidance, large gas projects sanctioned and positive '27 growth indications.

items.title: Global Theme Machine: Fossil Fuels Surge
items.summary: October marked a partial recovery in thematic performance after September's risk-off reversal. Ranking changes show an Earnings/Momentum-driven re-rating broadening, with Fossil Fuels moving to No. 9 in our rankings and Growth remaining the weakest-ranked factor within the theme universe.

items.title: Mexico Economics: Are Rates Headed for an Extended Pause?
items.summary: Mexico cut rates 25 basis points, below market expectations and our call for a hold. Forward guidance shifted materially, with commentary suggesting the cut was a fine-tuning adjustment. We look at policymakers' reasoning and why rates may now remain unchanged for some time.

items.title: Mexico Economics Weekly: Infrastructure-Plan Progress?
items.summary: Recent data suggest Mexico's infrastructure plan may be moving from announcement to execution. But private-sector participation remains key for the plan's success and still appears limited. We consider the potential impact of a broader pickup in private investment in this note.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: A Midterm Turn?
items.summary: Only time will tell what the U.S. midterms mean for the Middle East; energy prices would need to fall significantly to derail further ECB/UK hikes. Signaling by UK policymakers suggests a possible December hike; we enter Dec/Feb MPC SONIA flatteners. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Blue-Wave Help
items.summary: Emerging-markets central banks are shifting to a hawkish/neutral stance amid upside pressures in core inflation, domestic demand and energy inputs. The longer expensive energy inputs persist, the higher the risk of second-round CPI effects — an outcome policymakers must avoid at all costs.

items.title: Themes to Watch at Our 2026 China Conference
items.summary: Our flagship China Conference will be held Nov. 10-13 in Shanghai and Shenzhen. Our equity teams, economists and strategists highlight key themes to watch at this year’s conference, with our guide covering macroeconomic trends, policy direction, sector outlooks and investment ideas.
